activities.name: Settle into hotel and explore Hampi Bazaar – short stroll to Virupaksha Temple (heritage entry, free)
Guided sunrise visit to Virupaksha Temple – 45‑minute guide (captures early light for photography)

meals.breakfast: At hotel – simple South Indian spread (idli, chutney, filter coffee)

lunch.description: Vegetarian thali with rice, sambar, rasam, papad, and a sweet (served near the temple courtyard)
lunch.location_note: near Virupaksha Temple — approx 0.2 km from hotel

dinner.description: Ragi mudde with sambar and coconut chutney — local Karnataka comfort food
South Indian veg thali – assorted veg curries, rice, papad, and mango pickle
Rooftop restaurant with butter garlic prawns and masala potatoes – romantic ambience

days.notes: Easy first day to adjust; early breakfast, light lunch, and a relaxed evening. No strenuous walking.

activities.name: Bicycle‑rented tour of Royal Enclosure – Lotus Mahal, Elephant Stables, and Queen’s Bath (flat terrain, easy pace)
Coracle crossing to Hippie Island – short river ride for sunset photo‑ops

meals.breakfast: At hotel – poha with peanuts and a cup of chai

lunch.description: Masala dosa with coconut chutney and a side of potato fry (served near the Royal Enclosure entrance)
lunch.location_note: near Lotus Mahal — approx 0.5 km from bicycle drop‑off

dinner.description: Bisi bele bhath with crunchy papad and a side of cucumber raita
Veg thali with dal, rice, beans curry, and jaggery dessert
Boutique garden dining – paneer tikka, naan, and glass of local wine

days.notes: Mid‑day heat mitigated by staying in shade; coracle ride scheduled after 4 PM to avoid peak sun.

activities.name: Electric‑cart ride to Vittala Temple – explore Stone Chariot and musical pillars (cart mandatory)
Matanga Hill sunset trek – short, steep climb for panoramic shots (fit moderate pace)

meals.breakfast: At hotel – upma with grated coconut and a glass of fresh orange juice

lunch.description: Rice bowls with tangy avarekalu chutney and a side of fried okra (served near Vittala entrance)
lunch.location_note: near Stone Chariot — approx 1 km from cart drop‑off

dinner.description: Mysore masala dosa with coriander chutney and a bowl of sweet mango lassi
Family‑style veg thali — dal tadka, rice, mixed veg, and payasam
Elegant terrace dinner – grilled fish, herb quinoa, and dessert tiramisu

days.notes: Cart fee includes round‑trip; carry water for the hill trek. Evening light ideal for silhouette photography.

activities.name: Leisurely walk to Hemakuta Hill – gentle slopes, quick photo stops (no guide needed)
Return transfer to Hosapete railway station (taxi) for departure

meals.breakfast: At hotel – fresh fruit salad with yogurt and a cup of filter coffee

lunch.description: Veg pulao with cucumber raita and a sweet coconut laddu (served near Hemakuta viewpoint)
lunch.location_note: near Hemakuta Hill — approx 1.2 km from hotel

dinner.description: Traditional Karnataka-style rotti with brinjal curry and beetroot pachadi
Comfort veg thali – rice, sambar, mixed veg, and rice pudding
Fine‑dining experience – lamb rogan josh, saffron rice, and chocolate mousse

days.notes: Final day kept light for smooth departure; no long walks after lunch.

warnings: Coracle fare inflation: operators may quote ₹200‑500 per person; stick to the main ghat near Virupaksha Temple where competition keeps fares close to the official ₹30‑₹50 rate.
Electric cart is mandatory for Vittala Temple; walking the 1.5 km access road is prohibited, so factor the ₹50 per person fee into your budget.
Bicycle rentals are suitable only for flat zones like the Royal Enclosure; avoid using them on steep or uneven granite paths (e.g., Matanga Hill).
January mornings are crisp but midday sun can still be strong on exposed boulders; carry water, a hat, sunscreen, and limit continuous outdoor exposure between 10 AM‑4 PM.

Coracle fare inflation on Tungabhadra: operators at the Hampi–Virupapur Gaddi crossing quote ₹200–500 per person for the 5‑minute ride, while the government‑fixed rate is ₹30–50 one‑way. Mitigation: cross at the main ghat near Virupaksha Temple where competition holds fares closer to the official rate; always agree the price before boarding.

Heat exposure on exposed granite surfaces: even in cooler months (January) sun can cause heat exhaustion, especially for anyone carrying equipment or children. Mitigation: carry water, ORS, wear a hat, apply sunscreen, and limit midday exposure (plan visits 8‑10 AM or after 4 PM).

Stroller impracticality on graded gravel paths: most heritage zones have uneven stone/gravel, making strollers difficult to manoeuvre. Mitigation: use a carrier or rent a bicycle for flat sections; reserve a stroller only for paved hotel grounds.
Auto‑rickshaw pricing: ₹15–20 per km; half‑day heritage tour (Vittala + Royal Enclosure) ₹600–900. Confirm rates before hiring to avoid tourist‑spot inflation.
Electric cart mandatory at Vittala Temple costs ₹50 per person; no walking on the 1.5 km access road is allowed, so factor this into your budget.
Bicycle rental is ₹100–150 per day but only suitable for flat zones; avoid on the boulder‑laden trails of Hemakuta Hill or Matanga Hill.
Dining options are largely vegetarian in the heritage zone; non‑vegetarian meals and alcohol are only available on Hippie Island. Carry some packaged snacks if you require specific dietary items.
personalization_notes: Heritage focus: each day centers on iconic Hampi monuments, matching your interest in history and photography.
Moderate pace: activities limited to two per day with built‑in rest periods, ideal for a couple wanting to explore without rushing.
Budget‑friendly selections: accommodation budget tier, affordable meals, and selective premium dining for memorable evenings.
